newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Lockheed Martin in Russain joint venture.
newsitem.headline: Lockheed Martin in Russain joint venture.

text.p: Lockheed Martin Corp and Russia's the Intersputnik International Organisation of Space Commmunications said on Monday they would team up to launch satellites for global communications services.
Officials of the two companies told a news conference they would set up a joint venture company to be called Lockheed Martin Intersputnik Ltd (LMI) with headquarters in London.
They said the first satellite, a Lockheed Martin A-2100, would be launched in the last quarter of 1998.
The officials declined to offer any further details or say how much the two companies were investing.
"Money is a matter of the future," said Intersputnik dirctor general Gennady Kudryavtsev.
